notes.title: The Graphics Driver Update
notes.content:
Welcome to update 0.8! For the longest time I have wanted to completely redo the lighting in the game. Not only did I always feel like it wasn't the best lighting (especially the shadows), but it also contributed over 700MBs of the game's file size. After yearly attempt for the past few years, I have finally succeeded in not only reducing the file size but also improving the quality of lights and shadows. 

With the new lightmaps the game's filesize has reduced from 1.5GBs to just a tad below 1GB. But that's not the only change in this update, so let us get right to the changelog. 

[u][b]Major Changes[/b][/u]
[list]
[*] Complete Overhaul of Lighting
[*] Upgraded to a new Rendering Pipeline
[*] Replaced the Outline System
[/list]

[b][u]Minor Changes[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Updated to a new version of Unity
[*] Split grouped meshes into individual objects for optimization
[*] Optimizations across the game
[*] Minor changes to the Tutorial
[*] Further improvements to controller support
[/list]

[b][u]Bug Fixes[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed issues with Rubber Duck not always launching players
[*] Fixed levels 19-30 sometimes returning to main menu on finish
[*] Fixed & adjusted colliders on the Aeroplane
[/list]

If you find any bugs please do report them either in the Steam Discussions or over on the [url=https://discord.gg/tZRD9dgMx7]Fishagon Discord[/url]!

And with that we continue on the road to 1.0. I'm not going to give a self-imposed deadline on it this time around. It will come when it comes realistically. 

I will say the next update will build upon the changes of this update. There will be new objects to use in the level editor thanks to the mesh group splitting. The tutorial will receive an entire overhaul. 

Along with those changes next update we will be aiming to have official controller support & Steam Deck Verified. I estimate once those things are achieved we will be about an update away from full release. 

----

Also if you haven't seen we also released a free online party game about movies! Check it out below. 

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1792500/Boring_Movies/

In the future we will probably release a custom secret Minibot avatar for owners of this game to use on Boring Movies.

Thanks for reading and hope you enjoy the update!

notes.title: The 99% Calibration Update
notes.content:
Welcome to update 0.7! This is the final minor version release before 1.0. Train Your Minibot now has 30 total levels as I had always hoped to include. As well all known bugs have been fixed, the UI has been improved, and performance has been significantly increased (Steam Deck is quite a fun way to play).

I am extremely proud of the current state of the game and I hope you enjoy it as much as I have over the years. Although, this is not the end of development on TYM; below the patch notes I have included the roadmap to 1.0 if you are interested. 

[u][b]Major Changes[/b][/u]
[list]
[*][b] 12 NEW LEVELS ADDED[/b] bringing the game to a total of 30 levels!
[*] New Object Selection System, now raycasts from camera to finger tip instead of detection under the hand
[/list]

[u][b]Minor Changes[/b][/u]
[list]
[*] Reworked the "Floor is Lava" system for more accurate detection
[*] Further improved the In-Game Button Scaling
[*] Improved the Level Editor menu UI
[*] Minibot ragdoll effect has been greatly improved
[*] Improved the logic of the Mute button on Main Menu
[/list]

[u][b]Bug Fixes[/b][/u]
[list]
[*] An edge-case where Duck place-able became impossible to select
[*] Wind would push Minibot off Start while placing objects
[*] Minibot could be pushed off Finish
[*] Locked Levels can no longer be selected
[*] Cardboard Bottom Flaps will no longer occasionally kill Minibot
[*] Workshop level preview images will no longer show Aeroplane route
[*] Cleanup of base game level preview images
[*] The initial resolution setting will no longer set to the lowest supported value
[/list]

If you find any bugs please do report them either in the Steam Discussions or over on the [url=https://discord.gg/tZRD9dgMx7]Fishagon Discord[/url]!

[u][b]Roadmap to 1.0[/b][/u]
[list]
[*] Reordering all 30 levels by difficulty & learning curve
[*] Improved Controller Support
[*] Steam Deck Verified
[*] Complete Rework of Lights
[*] Expanded Settings Menus
[/list] 

These are the final four items I have planned for the 1.0 Update. 

The levels are currently in the order they were added to the game. Some of the final 12 levels that were included in this update are easier than earlier levels, but provide a better learning curve to some of the mechanics (especially the Aeroplane). 1.0 will reset unlocked levels unfortunately, but it is necessary for a better first-time player experience. 

Controller Support Improvements and Steam Deck verification are high priorities for the game. When I bring the game to conventions, this is how the game is played and I have received a lot of feedback on ways to improve this experience.

The lighting currently in the game makes up majority of the game disk space. Almost 700MBs of the game is dedicated to light bakes. And honestly, the shadows are not looking the best they could. I want to improve the overall visual quality of the game, reduce the file size, and make shadows as visually clear as possible (after all, shadows are a great landing indicator). 

And finally the settings menu currently is adequate, but do not allow you to fine-tune your graphics. This is a minor thing overall, but one that I believe any modern game should support. 

Have thoughts or suggestions on how to improve the game? Click that Discord link above and let me know! This is the final push to Full Release!

Lastly... When? The current goal is [b]June 20th[/b].

This is a smaller update than last, but it includes some crucial fixes that weren't apparent until we were testing one of the new upcoming levels. This update is a byproduct of the push to finish Train Your Minibot's levels. 

[u][b]Major Changes[/b][/u]
[list]
[*] Added Coyote Time! (note it's quite minor and only to cover very slight delay of input, I'm dedicated to keeping this a very precise platformer.)
[/list]

[u][b]Minor Changes[/b][/u]
[list]
[*] Movement Acceleration and Deceleration to smooth the animations
[*] Soda Particles have been overhauled
[*] Jenga blocks placed on RC trucks are now ridable
[/list]

[u][b]Bug Fixes[/b][/u]
[list]
[*] A very specific scenario we discovered while developing one of the final levels showed how the Retry and Puzzle Pause menus to overlap. This has been fixed, but also probably wasn't possible in the previous public builds.
[*] Push Currents no longer can push Minibot when he isn't in platformer mode
[/list]

notes.title: The Firmware Update
notes.content:
Hey! This is a big update; especially for bugs. This is the first update that will come over the next few months as we approach full release out of early access.

And I know some are wondering why this major update doesn't include any new levels? I've always wanted to launch with a total of 30 levels and that was before I even added an in-game level editor. 30 levels is still the release goal however! And good news the final 12 levels will be added to the game very soon. 

A professional level designer has been hired to assist me in finally getting these levels made. We are already putting the finishing touches on 3 of them and within the next month we should have all 12 in the game!

Also as a small note: the [url=https://open.spotify.com/album/3JYPYX5TgT3mqoxnt0CYDN?si=9UEpINK1RsGLB4VLZX0loA]Train Your Minibot OST is now on Spotify[/url] (and Pandora / other music streaming services)!!! 

[u][b]Major Changes[/b][/u]
[list]
[*] Updated Unity version from 2018 to 2022 LTS & 64bit executable
[*] Massive optimizations for better performance on low-end machines
[*] Added Particle Effects to Fans to Clearly Show the Harzard
[*] UI now scales and reacts better on different aspect ratios (specifically Ultra-Wide is now playable)
[*] Open Soda cans are now treated as a Movable object for levels (allowing more level design possibilities)
[/list]

[u][b]Minor Changes[/b][/u]
[list]
[*] Audio button on the task bar now mutes / unmutes audio
[*] Changed the jet booster particle effect
[*] Adjusted the finger to object selection zone (this is a continuous testing feature)
[/list]

[u][b]Bug Fixes[/b][/u]
[list]
[*] Power of Alignment Fixed (the weird drift you would see jumping from record players or planes)
[*] Wind Direction from fans assumed x-axis alignment now is direction-based
[*] Level Editor Bounding Boxes will no longer pulsate 
[*] Movable Record Players will no longer float off the ground when placed
[*] Mouse Traps weren't always triggering and when they did it they didn't animate
[/list]

If you find any bugs please do report them either in the Steam Discussions or over on the [url=https://discord.gg/tZRD9dgMx7]Fishagon Discord[/url]!

- Fixed the SFX Volume Slider from spamming the audio clip
- Switched Level Selection from the "Thumbnail" to the entire "Level Object"
- Adjusted the puzzle piece selection zone (will further tune this)

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1802750/Train_Your_Minibot_Soundtrack/]The OST has been launched on Steam for free by the way! [/url]

notes.title: The Reboot Update
notes.content:
Hey guys! It has been quite awhile since the last update. I have put off doing this update for quite awhile because I wanted to include some new levels along with it. 

Unfortunately, due to this delay in updating... I'm not exactly sure which of the bugs were fixed since I last updated, but there was a lot of them! 

So you should now find that the game is a lot more stable and you'll be running into a lot less bugs. 

The two new levels (Level 17 and 18) have been added to the game, they aren't as hard as some of the other levels which has me thinking that before full release I will most likely reorder the levels which will reset everyone's progress. 

Also I just want to let everyone know that the Train Your Minibot OST will be releasing in about 2 weeks, everyone who owns the game will be getting the soundtrack for free!

Looking forward to developing more levels prior to full release. If any bugs are encountered, please report them to the discussion board, thank you.

notes.title: Custom Levels with Steam Workshop Support & Tutorial Update
notes.content:
[u][b]Major Updates[/b][/u]
[list]
[*] Custom Level Editor
[*] Steam Workshop Support
[/list]

This is a pretty big update for Train Your Minibot and I'm super happy to announce that it includes a new custom level editor for anyone to design, play, and share their own levels to the community. This is obviously a major update for the game as it greatly expands the possibilities as it allows for more unrealistic levels that don't fit the game's theme (such as fun physics defying obstacles or full room exploration levels), but also these are the types of features that ensure the game can always continue to have new content. 

As well, the previous workflow for building levels in the Unity IDE was actually a lot more tedious than it is to build in this new level editor. So moving forward all the built-in official levels will also be designed using this level editor so I should be able to get new levels for everyone to play with a shorter turn-around time. 

And to kick off the Community Levels I've uploaded the first physics defying level aptly named "[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2588894929]CrazyPhysics[/url]".

[u][b]Quality of Life Improvement[/b][/u]
[list]
[*] Tutorial
[*] New Sensitivity & Minibot Zoom Defaults
[/list]

I've noticed from watching let's play YouTube videos that some players were confused about the game's controls or how to handle specific obstacles/mechanics. So I've added in new pop-up prompts that will instruct the user of the controls in the first level. Then moving forward will have prompts giving some guidance on a few of the different obstacles as they appear in the levels. 

As well I've adjusted the defaults for the mouse sensitivities and the level of camera zoom when controlling the minibot. It seems a lot of players have much higher DPI settings than I personally use, so I've adjusted the default to match more of the playerbase initially (this can still be changed in the Pause settings while playing). As well there is a tutorial prompt about this while playing for anyone that still finds it too fast or too slow. 

[u][b]Original Soundtrack[/b][/u]
[list]
[*] 3 new tracks!
[/list]

Lastly I'm excited to say that three new tracks have been added to the soundtrack by Train Your Minibot's OST team, the amazing composer [url=https://twitter.com/Sanityzermusic]Joshua Hunt[/url] (Composer) and Jordan Barillaro (Mixing/Mastering). 

This update brings the soundtrack up to 6 total tracks with a total runtime of 16 minutes. The current plan is to have a total of 14 tracks by full release!

notes.title: Preview Branch: Level Editor & Workshop Support
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

Sorry for the delay in updating, I'm a bit behind schedule but a lot of life events have taken me away from being able to work on the game as much as I would like. However, I have found enough time to finish the level editor for the most part and have it integrated into Steam Workshop. 

[b]New Features[/b]
[list]
[*] Create/Edit Custom Levels
[*] Upload Levels to Steam Workshop
[*] Subscribe and Play Anyone's Levels
[*] Achievement to Play 1 Custom Level
[/list]

You can checkout the physics defying custom level [url=https://steamcommunity.com/workshop/filedetails/?id=2588894929]I uploaded here.[/url] Note, no official levels will have physics defying layout.

I should note that you will need to go to the game in your Library and click "Properties" -> "Betas" -> Select "preview" from the dropdown. 

This feature will release in version 0.3 when the tutorial system is finished as well any bugs found in the system are fixed between now and then. 

Let me know your feedback on the system!

notes.title: Early Access Launch & Roadmap
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

Let me introduce myself; I'm Sky and I'm the solo developer that created Train Your Minibot. This project has been off and on for the past few years as I've debated when I wanted to take the large step into releasing my first paid game. 

Train Your Minibot is to the point now that I'm proud to put it on Steam and start receiving the communities' feedback on how to improve and progress the game forward to a full release. Hence, we are now entering Early Access. 

However, I'm not a fan of games sitting in Early Access for years and therefore am promising that Train Your Minibot will be here only as long as you guys feel it needs to mature into a full release. You can read my proposed roadmap [url=https://trello.com/b/7VJxCb7G/train-your-minibot-roadmap]here on Trello[/url] to see my current timeline up to Full Release in December 2021. 

Train Your Minibot is a puzzle platformer and as much as I know level content is important, the most important thing for this community will be the ability to create your own levels and share them on the Steam Workshop. Currently, I hope to release the Level Editor in August with version 0.3 (this is 0.2.0 right now)! But don't worry, I'll also be creating more main set levels as well, albeit a quicker pace since I can also utilize the level editor. 

I hope this process can integrate your feedback as much as possible. I've created a Discord where you can reach me personally to discuss ideas for mechanics, levels, or even to just report a bug. You can also check out my other projects there as I post updates / prototypes. 

https://www.discord.gg/RBPesMj

Lastly, I just want to say thanks to everyone that purchases Train Your Minibot, gifts it to a friend, or even just shares a link to it on social media. It means a lot to me and I hope the game can bring you some enjoyment.
